title: The Loud knock at the door
subtitle: 音乐之声 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 音乐之声（文学艺术与体育·音乐与表演）
meta: 主题语境：音乐之声（文学艺术与体育·音乐与表演）　|　核心词汇：loud　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 loud 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1950 the craftsman wrote of ① a loud knock at the door in the ledger, and everybody in the workshop said at once that it was ② louder than the one named there the year before. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the craftsman, who never explained anything, had done it year after year and gone home; it was the loud ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the loudest knock at the door anybody in the workshop had ever seen, or so the ledger for August 1944 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too loud to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the apprentice who had come to help; the loud ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the tool at the far bench, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a loud crowd in the yard, and said that no apprentice in his right mind would call it ⑥ as loud as the crowd in the yard they had once had in the old workshop. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was loud or not, and he said so.

By 1957 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the ledger. What the line asked for was ⑦ something loud, and nothing besides. The apprentice from the next workshop called the whole plan ⑧ quite loud; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the ledger kept the names of the loud ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1960, for the whole place, she wrote of another loud knock at the door in the same ledger, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ louder than anybody had expected. ⑩ The loudest crowd in the yard in the whole workshop, she said in 1962, was the one she could never quite name; the loud ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 大声（前置定语 a loud knock at the door：1950 年匠人在工料簿里记下的那件大声的敲门声）
B. adj. 大声／喧闹（比较级 louder than：文中两处，一处比响亮的敲门声，一处比预想）
C. adj. 大声／喧闹（最高级 the loudest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 大声（表语 too loud to do：母亲觉得它太大声，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 喧闹（前置定语 a loud crowd in the yard：叔叔把整件事称作一桩喧闹的人群）
F. adj. 喧闹（同级比较 as loud as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩院里喧闹的人群相比）
G. adj. 喧闹（后置定语 something loud：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 喧闹（受程度副词修饰 quite loud：那位学徒的评价）

items.q: a loud knock at the door
the loudest knock at the door anybody
a loud crowd in the yard
The loudest crowd in the yard in

answers.why: loud 意为“大声”，1950 年匠人在工料簿里记下的是“一件大声的敲门声”，此处作前置定语 a loud knock at the door。
loud 意为“大声”，此处用比较级 louder than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
loud 意为“大声”，工料簿上 八月 那行字说它是工坊里最大声的一件，故用最高级 the loudest knock at the door。
loud 意为“大声”，母亲认为这件东西“太大声了，谁也用不上”，too loud to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
loud 意为“喧闹”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩喧闹的人群”，此处作前置定语 a loud crowd in the yard。
loud 意为“喧闹”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩院里喧闹的人群一样喧闹”，同级比较用 as loud as。
loud 意为“喧闹”，工料簿上那半行字要的是“喧闹的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something loud。
loud 意为“喧闹”，邻工坊来的那位学徒认为这套计划“相当喧闹”，quite 修饰原级 loud。
loud 意为“喧闹”，1960 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要喧闹”，故用比较级 louder than。
loud 意为“喧闹”，母亲 1962 年说的是“整个工坊里最喧闹的那一桩”，故用最高级 the loudest crowd in the yard。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1950 年，匠人在工料簿里记下了一件大声的敲门声。（a loud knock at the door）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更大声。（louder than …）
母亲觉得它太大声，谁也用不上。（too loud to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩喧闹的人群。（a loud crowd in the yard）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩院里喧闹的人群一样喧闹。（as loud as …）
到了 1957 年，工料簿上只剩半行字：要的是一件喧闹的东西。（something loud）
answers: In 1950 the craftsman wrote of a loud knock at the door in the ledger.
Everybody said it was louder than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too loud to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a loud crowd in the yard.
He said nobody would call it as loud as the crowd in the yard they had once had.
By 1957 the ledger asked for nothing but something loud.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 loud 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1950 the craftsman wrote of a loud knock at the door in the ledger, and nobody forgot it.
It was the loudest knock at the door in the workshop, or so the ledger says.
My mother thought it too loud to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a loud crowd in the yard, and nobody argued with him.
The apprentice from the next workshop called the plan quite loud, and everybody laughed.
The loud ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
